/-!
# Conjecture 6.32

by O. V. Mel'nikov

Let $F_n$ be the free profinite group of finite rank $n > 1$. Is it true that for each
normal subgroup $N$ of the free profinite group of countable rank, there exists a normal
subgroup of $F_n$ isomorphic to $N$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.32»

open Filter Topology CategoryTheory

/-- A profinite group is free on a family indexed by $\iota$ if it has a family of generators
converging to the identity such that every family in a profinite group which converges to the
identity extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism.

For finite $\iota$, convergence along the cofinite filter is automatic. For $\iota = \mathbb{N}$,
it says that the sequence of generators converges to the identity. -/
def IsFreeProfiniteGroupOn (ι : Type) (G : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ι → G, Tendsto x cofinite (𝓝 1) ∧
    ∀ (H : ProfiniteGrp) (y : ι → H), Tendsto y cofinite (𝓝 1) →
      ∃! φ : G ⟶ H, ∀ i, φ (x i) = y i

/--
For every finite rank $n > 1$, is every closed normal subgroup $N$ of the free profinite
group of countable rank topologically isomorphic to a closed normal subgroup of the free
profinite group $F_n$ of rank $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.32» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 < n → ∀ (Fω Fn : ProfiniteGrp),
      IsFreeProfiniteGroupOn ℕ Fω → IsFreeProfiniteGroupOn (Fin n) Fn →
      ∀ N : Subgroup Fω, N.Normal → IsClosed (N : Set Fω) →
        ∃ M : Subgroup Fn, M.Normal ∧ IsClosed (M : Set Fn) ∧ Nonempty (N ≃ₜ* M) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.32»

The finite-rank group uses `Fin n`; convergence along the cofinite filter is then automatic. The countable-rank group uses `ℕ`, whose cofinite filter is `atTop`.

Quantified over bundled `ProfiniteGrp` representatives satisfying the universal property, since Mathlib has the category of profinite groups but no construction of free profinite groups. The claimed property is invariant under topological group isomorphism.
Interpreted “normal subgroup” in the profinite sense as a `Subgroup` that is both normal and closed.
Interpreted “isomorphic” as `Nonempty (N ≃ₜ* M)`, i.e. existence of a continuous multiplicative equivalence and therefore a topological group isomorphism.

# Conjecture 6.32

by O. V. Mel'nikov

Let $F_n$ be the free profinite group of finite rank $n > 1$. Is it true that for each normal
subgroup $N$ of the free profinite group of countable rank, there exists a normal subgroup of
$F_n$ isomorphic to $N$?

As usual in the theory of profinite groups, "normal subgroup" means closed normal subgroup and
"isomorphic" means isomorphic as topological groups.

The free profinite group of finite rank $n$ is the profinite completion
$\widehat{F_n} = \varprojlim F_n/N$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators, where $N$ ranges
over the normal subgroups of finite index of $F_n$. The free profinite group of countable rank
is the free profinite group on a countably infinite set of generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$
converging to $1$; it is the inverse limit $\varprojlim F/N$ of the finite quotients of the
free group $F$ on $x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$ by the normal subgroups $N$ of finite index that
contain all but finitely many of the generators $x_i$ (see Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*,
Section 3.3).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- [L. Ribes, P. Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-01642-4)
-/

open CategoryTheory

namespace Kourovka.«6.32»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- Given a family `S` of finite-index normal subgroups of a group `G`, the functor sending
`N ∈ S` to the finite group `G ⧸ N`, and an inclusion `N ≤ M` to the natural projection
`G ⧸ N → G ⧸ M`. -/
def quotientFunctor (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (hS : ∀ N ∈ S, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex) :
    S ⥤ FiniteGrp where
  obj N :=
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).1
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).2
    FiniteGrp.of (G ⧸ N.1)
  map {N M} f :=
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).1
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).2
    haveI := (hS M.1 M.2).1
    haveI := (hS M.1 M.2).2
    FiniteGrp.ofHom (QuotientGroup.map _ _ (.id _) (leOfHom f))
  map_id N :=
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).1
    ConcreteCategory.ext <| QuotientGroup.map_id _
  map_comp {N M K} f g :=
    haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).1
    haveI := (hS M.1 M.2).1
    haveI := (hS K.1 K.2).1
    ConcreteCategory.ext <| (QuotientGroup.map_comp_map
      _ _ _ (.id _) (.id _) (leOfHom f) (leOfHom g)).symm

/-- The completion of a group `G` with respect to a family `S` of finite-index normal subgroups
of `G`: the profinite group $\varprojlim_{N \in S} G/N$, where each finite quotient $G/N$ carries
the discrete topology. -/
def completion (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (hS : ∀ N ∈ S, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex) : ProfiniteGrp :=
  ProfiniteGrp.limit (quotientFunctor G S hS ⋙ forget₂ FiniteGrp ProfiniteGrp)

/-- The canonical homomorphism from `G` to its completion with respect to `S`. -/
def toCompletion (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (hS : ∀ N ∈ S, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex) :
    G →* completion G S hS where
  toFun g := ⟨fun N => haveI := (hS N.1 N.2).1; QuotientGroup.mk g, fun _ _ _ => rfl⟩
  map_one' := rfl
  map_mul' _ _ := rfl

/-- The profinite completion $\widehat{G} = \varprojlim G/N$ of a group `G`, where `N` ranges over
all normal subgroups of finite index of `G`. -/
def profiniteCompletion : ProfiniteGrp :=
  completion G {N | N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex} fun _ hN => hN

/-- The free profinite group $F_n$ of finite rank `n`: the profinite completion of the free
group on `n` generators. -/
def freeProfiniteGroup (n : ℕ) : ProfiniteGrp :=
  profiniteCompletion (FreeGroup (Fin n))

/-- The free profinite group $F_\omega$ of countable rank $\aleph_0$, i.e. the free profinite
group on a countably infinite set of generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$ converging to $1$.
It is the completion $\varprojlim F/N$ of the free group $F$ on $x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$, where
`N` ranges over the normal subgroups of finite index of $F$ containing all but finitely many of
the generators $x_i$ (equivalently, those `N` for which the map
$\{x_0, x_1, \ldots\} \cup \{1\} \to F/N$ is continuous). -/
def freeProfiniteGroupCountableRank : ProfiniteGrp :=
  completion (FreeGroup ℕ)
    {N | N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ {i | FreeGroup.of i ∉ N}.Finite} fun _ hN => ⟨hN.1, hN.2.1⟩

/-- The free profinite group of rank $0$ is the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20 22]
theorem subsingleton_freeProfiniteGroup_zero : Subsingleton (freeProfiniteGroup 0) :=
  ⟨fun x y => ProfiniteGrp.limit_ext _ x y fun N =>
    @Subsingleton.elim (FreeGroup (Fin 0) ⧸ N.1) QuotientGroup.mk_surjective.subsingleton _ _⟩

/-- The images in $F_\omega$ of the free generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$ converge to $1$. -/

theorem tendsto_toCompletion_of_cofinite :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun i : ℕ => toCompletion (FreeGroup ℕ) _ _ (FreeGroup.of i) :
        ℕ → freeProfiniteGroupCountableRank)
      Filter.cofinite (nhds 1) := by
  rw [tendsto_subtype_rng, tendsto_pi_nhds]
  intro N
  obtain ⟨_, _, hN⟩ := N.2
  rw [@nhds_discrete _ _ ⟨rfl⟩, Filter.tendsto_pure]
  refine hN.subset fun i hi => ?_
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
  intro h
  apply hi
  change (QuotientGroup.mk (FreeGroup.of i) : FreeGroup ℕ ⧸ N.1) = 1
  exact (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff _).mpr h

/--
Let $F_n$ be the free profinite group of finite rank $n > 1$. Is it true that for each normal
subgroup $N$ of the free profinite group of countable rank, there exists a normal subgroup of
$F_n$ isomorphic to $N$?

/--
A profinite group $F$ together with a map $\iota \colon X \to F$ is *the free profinite group
on $X$ (converging to $1$)* if $\iota$ converges to $1$, i.e. every neighbourhood of $1$ in $F$
contains $\iota(x)$ for all but finitely many $x \in X$, and every map $f \colon X \to G$
converging to $1$ into a profinite group $G$ extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F \to G$ with $\varphi \circ \iota = f$.

When $X$ is finite the convergence conditions are vacuous, and this is the usual universal
property of the free profinite group on $X$, i.e. of the profinite completion of the free
group on $X$. The free profinite group on $X$ is unique up to isomorphism of topological
groups, and its rank is the cardinality of $X$.
-/
structure IsFreeProfiniteGroupOn {X : Type*} {F : ProfiniteGrp.{u}} (ι : X → F) : Prop where
  /-- The generators `ι x` converge to `1`. -/
  tendsto_cofinite : Tendsto ι cofinite (𝓝 1)
  /-- Every map into a profinite group converging to `1` extends uniquely to a continuous
  homomorphism. -/

    ∃! φ : F →ₜ* G, ⇑φ ∘ ι = f

/-- The trivial profinite group is the free profinite group on the empty set. -/

theorem isFreeProfiniteGroupOn_empty :
    IsFreeProfiniteGroupOn (F := ProfiniteGrp.of Unit) Empty.elim where
  tendsto_cofinite := by simp
  existsUnique_lift G f _ := by
    refine ⟨1, funext fun x => x.elim, fun φ _ => ?_⟩
    ext x
    rw [Subsingleton.elim x 1]
    simp

normal subgroup $N$ of the free profinite group of countable rank, there exists a normal

by O. V. Mel'nikov

Let $F_n$ be the free profinite group of finite rank $n > 1$. Is every closed normal
subgroup of the free profinite group of countable rank topologically isomorphic to a
closed normal subgroup of $F_n$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«6.32»

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- A profinite group freely generated by a family indexed by `ι` that converges to the
identity along the filter `l`. The universal property only considers families in the
target that also converge to the identity along `l`. -/
def IsFreeProfiniteGroupOnFilter (P : ProfiniteGrp) {ι : Type*} (l : Filter ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ι → P, Tendsto x l (𝓝 1) ∧
    ∀ (G : ProfiniteGrp) (f : ι → G), Tendsto f l (𝓝 1) →
      ∃! φ : P ⟶ G, ∀ i, φ (x i) = f i

/-- A free profinite group of finite rank `n`. Using the bottom filter places no
convergence restriction on its `Fin n` generators or their images. -/
def IsFreeProfiniteGroupOfFiniteRank (P : ProfiniteGrp) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsFreeProfiniteGroupOnFilter P (⊥ : Filter (Fin n))

/-- A free profinite group of countable rank, with a countably infinite free generating
family converging to the identity. -/
def IsFreeProfiniteGroupOfCountableRank (P : ProfiniteGrp) : Prop :=
  IsFreeProfiniteGroupOnFilter P (cofinite : Filter ℕ)

/--
Is it true that, for every finite rank $n > 1$, each closed normal subgroup $N$ of the
free profinite group on a countably infinite family converging to $1$ is topologically
isomorphic to a closed normal subgroup of the free profinite group $F_n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.32» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 < n →
      ∀ (Fₙ Fω : ProfiniteGrp),
        IsFreeProfiniteGroupOfFiniteRank Fₙ n →
        IsFreeProfiniteGroupOfCountableRank Fω →
        ∀ N : ClosedSubgroup Fω, (N : Subgroup Fω).Normal →
          ∃ M : ClosedSubgroup Fₙ, (M : Subgroup Fₙ).Normal ∧ Nonempty (N ≃ₜ* M) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.32»
